mobile.computers.session_error_help: Your computer does not need to be reconfigured. Retry, or show the details for support.
mobile.computers.account_mismatch: This computer belongs to another Radient account, or was removed.
mobile.computers.account_help: Sign in with the account that owns it. If it was removed, choose another computer.
mobile.computers.billing_help: In the Radient console, open this tunnel's billing settings and activate remote access.
mobile.computers.disabled_help: Radient says this tunnel isn't active right now. Check its status in the Radient console.
mobile.computers.harness_help: In the Radient console, enable the Local Operator harness for this tunnel.
mobile.computers.connect_refused.title: Couldn't connect
mobile.computers.connect_refused.generic: The computer didn't accept the connection. Your address and password are still here, so check them and try again.
mobile.computers.connect_refused.passwor: The relay didn't accept that password. Check it and try again.
mobile.computers.storage_refused.with_co: This device's secure storage refused the request (code {code}). Try again, or reinstall the app if it keeps happening.
mobile.computers.storage_refused.no_code: This device's secure storage refused the request. Try again, or reinstall the app if it keeps happening.
mobile.computers.save_refused.title: Connected, but not saved
mobile.computers.save_refused.body: This device couldn't store the address and password securely. The connection works for now, but you'll need to enter them again after the app restarts.
mobile.computers.save_refused.body_with_: This device couldn't store the address and password securely (code {code}). The connection works for now, but you'll need to enter them again after the app restarts.
mobile.computers.wait.nothing_answered_h: Three minutes with no tunnel listed and no host answering. Check the command ran on the computer, then start again.
mobile.computers.wait.paused: Paused while the app is in the background. Reopen it to keep watching.
mobile.computers.wait.relay_version_sess: Its relay reports protocol version {version} and {sessions, plural, one {# running session} other {# running sessions}}.
mobile.computers.wait.relay_sessions: Its relay reports {sessions, plural, one {# running session} other {# running sessions}}.
mobile.computers.wait.host_answering: Waiting for your computer at {host} to answer. A provisioned route is not the same as a machine that is up.
mobile.computers.wait.answering: Waiting for your computer to answer.
mobile.computers.not_harness: This computer is not running the Local Operator harness.
mobile.computers.wait.listing: Waiting for Radient to list your computer…
mobile.computers.list.heading: Your computers
mobile.computers.remove.title: Remove this computer?
mobile.computers.remove.body: This removes it from the list on this phone. It does not touch the computer, its tunnel, or your account.
mobile.computers.paths.radient_body: Needs a Radient account. Radient runs the tunnel for you and gives you a private, authenticated URL, so there is nothing to configure on this phone and no relay password to keep.
mobile.computers.paths.own_body: The advanced path: you publish your computer yourself, through a tunnel you run, and paste its address here. No Radient account is needed at any point, and you keep the password.
mobile.computers.billing_inactive: Billing for this tunnel is inactive, so remote access will be refused.
mobile.computers.banner.unreachable_stal: Radient could not be reached, so this list may be out of date.
mobile.computers.banner.unreachable_empt: Radient could not be reached to list your computers. Check this device's connection.
mobile.computers.banner.unreadable_stale: Radient's answer could not be read, so this list may be out of date.
mobile.computers.banner.unreadable_empty: Radient's answer could not be read, so your computers could not be listed.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.title: Your own tunnel
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.intro: No Radient account is needed for any of this. You publish the relay on your own computer through a tunnel you control, and the app talks to it through the address you paste below.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_compute: The relay binds loopback only, so this is the machine that has to run it. Leave it awake while you use the app.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_hin: Needed only for an address over http, which sends the password in the clear
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_on_: On: the relay password and everything you send cross this network unencrypted. Only do this on a network you trust.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.insecure_off: Over http:// your relay password crosses the network in the clear, so it is off unless you turn it on. Use https:// whenever the address supports it.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.unencrypted_: Turn the opt-in on to use it, or give an https:// address — a tunnel normally prints one.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.private_host: This address is on your own network, so the exposure is limited to it.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.public_host: This address is not a private one — anything between this phone and it can read the password.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.step_test_he: This makes a real request through your tunnel before anything is saved.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.security_bod: You are putting your own computer on the internet, and the relay password is the only thing standing in front of it. Prefer HTTPS, use a tunnel that offers its own authentication where yours does, and change the password in your computer's Phone access settings if it has been shared. Anyone with that password and your URL can drive the sessions on that machine.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.need_address: Paste your tunnel's address to continue.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.need_test: Test the connection first — a tunnel that has not answered once is not one to save.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.foreground_l: Or run it in the foreground
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.install_note: macOS: writes the supervised daemon, generates the portal password and keeps it in your keychain.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.foreground_n: Any other platform, or when you would rather watch the log. It serves {address}, loopback only.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.check_note: Health, the state of the auth gate, and the sessions the phone will see.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.rotate_note: Asks you interactively, so the value never reaches a shell history or a process list. This is the password the app asks for below.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.cloudflare_n: Free and needs no account for a quick tunnel. It prints the {scheme} URL to paste below.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.ngrok_note: Needs an ngrok account. It prints the {scheme} URL to paste below.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.tunnel_rule: Any tunnel works as long as it forwards a public HTTPS URL to {address} on that computer.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_sess: Connected — you can see {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_pass: That password was not accepted. Check the relay password on the computer.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_forb: That tunnel refused the app. If you put an access policy or a login page in front of it, allow the app through; the relay itself also refuses requests from any other origin, so make sure the tunnel forwards straight to {address} rather than to a dashboard or another app.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_offl: The tunnel answered, but the relay behind it is not. On that computer: {command}
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_tls: That tunnel's certificate was rejected. Use the {scheme} address the tunnel printed, choose a tunnel with a certificate a phone will trust, or replace a self-signed certificate on the one you run — the app will not skip the check.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_host: That host name could not be found. Check the address for a typo, and that the tunnel still publishes that name.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_unre: The address could not be reached. Check the URL is the public one your tunnel printed, and that the tunnel is still running.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_time: That address did not answer within {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}. Check the tunnel is running and the computer is awake.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_loca: Nothing answered at that address on this network. Check the computer is awake and running the relay. If both are true, it may be the local-network permission: allow Local Operator under Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network, then tap {action}.
Nothing answered at that address on this network. Check the computer is awake and running the relay, then tap {action}.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.verdict_refu: That address answered, but not in a way this app understands.
mobile.computers.own_tunnel.password_slo: This phone keeps one relay password, and it belongs to another address. Enter this computer's password, test it, then save. It replaces the other one.
This phone has no relay password saved. Enter this computer's password, test it, then save.
This phone's saved relay password is for this address. Test it, then save.
mobile.computers.setup.open_settings: On your computer, open Local Operator → Settings → Phone access → Set up.
mobile.computers.setup.list_updates: Come back here when it's done — this list updates by itself.
